exact_text:
Anytime you see wild new
highs (or lows) that aren’t accompanied by wild new high volume, be suspicious of the staying power of the move.
added_conditions: volume, which is usually low at an exhaustion gap

exact_text:
A runaway gap or common gap is another matter. Demand for the stock is
normal and not under the influence of news or changing conditions, so the
gap may be filled by bargain hunters.
added_conditions: a breakaway gap often does not return to fill the gap for many months or years, if ever

exact_text:
When you see a doji after a prolonged uptrend, the doji may mean that the
buyers are coming to the end of their bullish enthusiasm.
added_conditions: a doji is interpreted in the context of the pattern of the preceding bars

exact_text:
If the price move is a downtrend, the dragonfly may mean that
buyers are emerging and the downtrend may be ending.
added_conditions: interpretation of the dragonfly depends on what bar patterns precede it

exact_text:
A long black bar implies panic selling. But to interpret the white bar as an
ending burst in an uptrend is more subtle.
An engulfing pattern signals the reversal of a trend.

After the two white candles
comes a bearish engulfing candle, a reversal warning that this up move may
be ending.

A dead-cat bounce is a peculiar continuation pattern that looks like a reversal at the beginning, with a sizeable upward retracement of a down move,
but then fades back to the same downward direction.
added_conditions: a dead-cat bounce occurs only in down moves

exact_text:
The bounce upward averages 19 percent from the lowest low.
✓ The average decline from the top of the retracement bounce is 15 percent and lasts an average of three months.
added_conditions: the pattern fails to deliver an additional decline only 10 percent of the time

added_parameters.name: average bounce size from lowest low
average decline from top of retracement

exact_text:
You will run into situations where a breakout is not respected and the price resumes the direction
it was headed in the first place.
added_conditions: a breakout is not always respected

exact_text:
Another type of measured move is when a price repeats the extent of a first
move after a retracement.
added_conditions: the price resumes the trend at the same slope and to the same extent after the retracement

exact_text:
This touch-bounce is confirmation that
the line is more than just a line and is a true trendline.
added_conditions: the line becomes a trendline only when another daily price low touches the line and bounces off it

exact_text:
Traders know that others
will exit at a level of (say) 8 to 10 percent or 25 percent under the peak, and
will sell the security specifically to get everyone else to exit, whereupon
they’re able to buy the security at
added_conditions: the well-known stop rules become self-fulfilling because many traders use them

exact_text:
The support line entry rule says: Buy on the third touch of the support line
by the low of a price bar.
added_conditions: in some securities, including foreign exchange (FX), traders push the price to break the support line but then buy it back so that the close remains over the support line

exact_text: When the support line does hold, the traders who were selling become big buyers.
added_conditions: this trend end may or may not be true; the move can continue after the line was broken

exact_text:
But it’s the best place to reenter an existing trend
(with an exit planned just below using a stop-loss order in case it doesn’t
work).
added_conditions: if the trend resumes it will exceed the previous high

exact_text:
At the pivot point, the crowd itself realizes that it has gone to an extreme,
and it reacts by heading in the opposite direction.

If the price had been in a downtrend, this wild increase in volume
means that the crowd is throwing in the towel and exiting en masse.
added_conditions: the same principle applies to a volume spike as the price makes new highs: the crowd has exhausted its supply of cash

added_parameters.name: volume spike threshold
added_parameters.value: double or more the size of volume on the preceding days

exact_text:
The lines stop being hypothetical and become actual support and resistance
when the next high or low touches the extended line but doesn’t break it,
validating the extension process.
added_conditions: a channel line is correctly drawn when a third relative high or low makes a touch of the line but doesn't cross it

exact_text:
When a new price touches the channel top or bottom, but then retreats,
you believe that the channel limits are correctly drawn and valid — and
will likely work next time, too.
added_conditions: the more often a price touches a support or resistance line but doesn't cross it, the more reliable the line

exact_text:
Buy near the channel bottom and sell near the channel top — over and
over again, as long as the channel lasts.
added_conditions: only as long as the channel remains in place and you are able to sell near the resistance line

exact_text:
The term smart money refers to traders who see the exhaustion of a price
move ahead of the other traders.
added_conditions: they are alert to the moment when the crowd realizes it has taken a price too far and reacts violently in the other direction
